title: Kettlebell Single-Leg RDL
summary: A one-leg hinge with a kettlebell, which loads the hamstrings and glutes at long length and challenges your balance.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.9 for hamstrings (main mover): each working set adds 0.9 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.
Library rating 0.9 for glutes (main mover): each working set adds 0.9 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.3 for abductors (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly abductors total.
Library rating 0.25 for adductors (minor): each working set adds 0.25 of a set to the weekly adductors total.
Library rating 0.25 for lower back (minor): each working set adds 0.25 of a set to the weekly lower back total.

setup.text: Stand on one leg with a bell in the opposite hand.
Hinge forward as your free leg reaches back, until your hamstring stretches.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.

form_cues.cue: Hinge forward as the free leg rises
Stand by driving the hip forward
Keep your hips square to the floor.

mistakes.text: Opening the hips toward the ceiling.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: More stable, Both sides together.
Swap sheet: More stable, Both sides together, Loads the spine.
Swap sheet: More stable, Both sides together, Less systemic fatigue.
